reason: The cited evidence (E1) confirms that IrOsPtPdRhRuOs catalyzes ethanol oxidation via a 12-electron process, unlike single metals, and notes that heterogeneity in HEAs enables tuning of selectivity. However, it does not provide direct evidence for the specific mechanistic claims about ensemble effects, ligand/strain modulation of adsorption energies, or the role of sluggish diffusion in suppressing coarsening. These key premises are therefore largely unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Atomically homogeneous mixing in PtPdRhRuIrOs creates a unique ensemble of active sites
This ensemble modulates adsorption energies of ethanol and intermediates via ligand and strain effects
The synergy facilitates simultaneous C–C bond cleavage and full 12-electron dehydrogenation
Sluggish diffusion inherent to HEA structure suppresses nanoparticle coarsening and degradation
Induced elemental segregation will reduce synergy, shifting oxidation to a 4-electron pathway and lowering durability
